notes:
ATTEMPT 3 (final) - adversarial re-read of candidate-3.png against /images/blueprints/supplier/9e99ee8084ba__0541__Left_bttn_hole.jpg.

WHAT THE DRAWING SHOWS, READ DIRECTLY: a jacket front upper - collar band, collar, and two notch lapels forming a long narrow V down the chest. On the lapel that appears on the RIGHT of the frame there is one small red mark, high on the lapel and close to its outer edge, marking the buttonhole position. The lapel that appears on the LEFT of the frame carries NO mark of any kind. Total marked buttonholes: exactly one.

ADVERSARIAL COUNT CHECK ON THE RENDER: the frame-right lapel carries exactly ONE worked buttonhole, a clean cut slit with dense tonal oversewing, sitting high on the lapel near its outer edge. I searched the frame-left lapel specifically for a mirrored buttonhole and there is none - the only feature on it is the collar/lapel notch at the gorge, confirmed as a notch and not a buttonhole by its position (it mirrors the notch on the right lapel, far above the buttonhole height) and by its shape. Total buttonhole count in the render: exactly one, on the correct lapel. That is the whole meaning of the option and it is right.

THE ATTEMPT-3 CORRECTION WORKED. Attempt 2's only substantive complaint was that the tonal-on-tonal buttonhole read softly at 1k. The raking side light asked for in the attempt-3 correction resolved it: the slit now shows a distinct open aperture with the gimp standing in visible relief against the hopsack, identifiable within a second. Crucially the thread stayed TONAL NAVY - the correction did not tempt the generator into a contrast colour, which would have been a real error rather than an improvement.

HOSTILE CHECKS CLEAN: no red or coloured thread on either lapel; the red position mark in the drawing did NOT bleed into the cloth; no second buttonhole invented on the opposite lapel; lapel style is notch as drawn, not peak and not shawl; no necktie added; no numerals, units, arrows, leader lines, callouts, ruler ticks or labels; no watermark; plain neutral grey sweep with no location, props or scenery; no button-stance, pocket or vent geometry borrowed from a neighbouring option.

Only two minor observations remain, one a tiny off-subject shirt-collar speck and one the inherent flat-schematic-versus-worn-garment difference. Retry budget genuinely spent at attempt 3 of 3 with zero critical or major findings.
